summary: TheBarcode Lite 1.12.33 fixes stock quantity and monetary input validation across inventory, purchasing, production and payments.
notes: Fixed quantity validation: discrete stock accepts whole units, measured stock accepts decimals, and monetary inputs accept cents.
The local API now has up to 30 seconds to finish startup on slower devices.
When desktop startup fails but the local API is healthy, TheBarcode opens in the default browser and keeps the API running until the fallback window is closed.
Fixed the SQLite startup crash when background jobs resume after installation or restart.
Lite migrations check existing columns before changing schema, avoiding false error entries while preserving client data.
Visible grids page their rows; the Bills register fetches 50 records at a time and searches all bills on the local server.
Short-lived read caching combines duplicate requests and clears on business changes; routine polling pauses when the page is hidden.
SQLite Lite uses write-ahead logging and new non-destructive search and transaction indexes.
Historical sales imports and owner backups run as persistent jobs with progress, retry and clear failure messages.
Owner and manager System logs show database, sync-queue, read-cache and slow-request health.
Accounting trial balance totals run in the database; source-journal reconciliation avoids duplicate concurrent work.
Each historical sale row receives a unique receipt number.
TheBarcode Lite uses its private local SQLite database and does not install or require PostgreSQL.
Lite upgrades retain the existing TheBarcode or Dukora Lite database in the user's local app-data folder.
The installer stops safely when it detects a PostgreSQL edition configuration, leaving that database untouched instead of showing stale SQLite data.
Item setup now saves creates and edits locally and synchronizes them when the connection returns.
Inventory refreshes preserve pending offline sales and stock movements without losing or double-applying stock changes.
Owner and manager-only System logs show server outcomes, failures, duration, record counts and local sync errors.
Unused setup items can be permanently deleted with a recorded reason; items with operational history remain archive-only.
Deposit and credit orders now default a blank expected delivery date to the posting date and time so they are always stored in Orders and the delivery calendar.
The rule-based assistant can summarize inventory, stock inflows and outflows for day, week, month or quarter periods and compare them with the previous equivalent period.
TheBarcode assistant is now a compact animated floating icon positioned above bottom action rows so it stays available without blocking checkout controls.
Accounting journal history marks superseded correction snapshots in red with strike-through; only the active snapshot feeds balances.
Held bills highlight products approaching their stock threshold and surface an urgency review action.
A deterministic, offline rule-based assistant answers workflow and FAQ questions with page-aware navigation.
Printer settings can inspect and cancel only TheBarcode receipt jobs in the selected Windows printer queue.
Dynamic item and supplier selectors support type-ahead search, and responsive layouts collapse safely on compact screens.
Order calendar entries are crossed out after payment, completion or cancellation while unresolved balances remain active.
Deposit and partial-payment receipts now separate the paid deposit from the outstanding balance, with balances highlighted in red in print preview.
Orders include a responsive delivery calendar with scheduled-order counts, month navigation and direct order drill-down.
Fulfillment statuses can be updated by assigned staff or owners/managers and each change is recorded in the audit trail.
Owner and manager-assigned permissions now authorize reports, audit, accounting, approvals, expenses and inventory independently of base staff roles.
Demo and live institution data remain strictly isolated across dashboards, bills, expenses, reports, insights and notifications.
Accounting journals, trial balance, financial position and operational corrections reconcile from live transactions.
Purchasing, stocktakes, lot-aware wastage and production runs update inventory, weighted cost, accounting and audit history transactionally.
Held bills support revisions, new products, approval workflows, cash or M-Pesa posting and explicit unpaid, paid or credit receipts.
Expenses support submission, approval, editing, payments, archival and authoritative notification clearing.
TheBarcode branding, theme-aware transparent artwork and Beyond Raw Data publisher identity are included in the installer.
The installer preserves the institution database, bundles WebView2 and the verified Xprinter driver, and creates the local server and print bridge.
Fixed an API startup failure caused by implicit request-body binding on the product DELETE endpoint.
Added an automated startup-route validation test so invalid API route bindings are caught before release packaging.
Font scaling, responsive touch layouts, full-screen mode, collapsible navigation and global grid search/sorting are included.
Production hardening adds live and database readiness checks, bounded API timeouts and backoff for offline synchronization retries.
Native startup now uses a service-aware launcher and detects incomplete legacy configuration before deciding whether SQLite migration is required.
Windows shortcuts target only the native launcher and printer executable; configuration runs during setup without creating a Defender-sensitive parameterized shortcut.
The native launcher no longer requests nested UAC elevation when setup is already elevated, preventing false configuration-cancelled errors.
